step1_summary.chief_complaint: Severe left-sided headache with visual disturbance and nausea
symptoms: Headache started suddenly this morning, about 4 hours ago
Headache severity rated 6/10 (less severe than past kidney stone pain)
Headache localized to left side of the head, not behind the eye
Visual disturbances described as blurred vision and zigzag lines
Dizziness on standing or moving, worsens with movement
Nausea and vomiting (vomited twice since onset)
Headache is new, never experienced before this intensity or nature
Paracetamol tried 3 hours ago without relief
vital_signs/exam_findings: No reported weakness, no gait abnormalities

V: Migraine with aura - Vascular dysregulation leading to headache and visual disturbances.
Stroke or TIA - sudden headache and vision symptoms could relate to vascular event, although no weakness or neurological signs reported.
I: Meningitis or encephalitis - headache, vomiting, and photophobia (unable to stand screens) could indicate CNS infection, but no fever or neck stiffness documented.
N: Brain tumor - new headache with visual symptoms raises concern, but no focal neurological signs and sudden onset less typical.
D: Hypothyroidism-related headache - family history, but no other symptoms or direct linkage documented.
I2: Medication side effect or overdose - none reported.
A: Migraine - typically an autonomic vascular/neurological disorder with aura causing visual symptoms and nausea.
T: Trauma - no history of head injury.
E: Hypertension-related headache - not documented but could cause sudden headache with nausea; no BP data available.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Sudden onset unilateral headache with visual disturbances (zigzag lines), nausea, vomiting, and family history of migraine strongly support typical migraine presentation.
supporting_evidence: Left-sided headache with blurred vision and zigzag lines
Headache is new, severe, and unilateral
Symptoms worsen with movement and light exposure (screen intolerance)
opposing_evidence: Migraine typically starts earlier in life; patient reports this is first time with migraine-like symptoms
